name: Ideology of the Chinese Communist Party
summary: The CCP's official ideology is Marxism-Leninism adapted to China, running through Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development and Xi Jinping Thought. It holds that the Party must lead everything, that the state is a people's democratic dictatorship, and that a socialist market economy with dominant public ownership is the path to national rejuvenation and, eventually, communism. It rejects liberal constitutionalism, separation of powers and multiparty democracy, and promotes whole-process people's democracy, common prosperity, cultural confidence and Sinicised religion.
scope: The current official line of the CCP as set out in the 2022 Party Constitution and Xi Jinping's report to the 20th National Congress, including its Mao and Deng antecedents. It excludes dissident Marxist, Maoist-revival and liberal reformist currents inside China, and many answers on social issues are inferred because the documents do not address them.

sources.title: Full text of the report to the 20th National Congress of the Communist Party of China
sources.author: Xi Jinping, via China Daily
sources.usedFor: Current programme on Party leadership, market role, Taiwan, religion, energy, security and foreign policy.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The 20th Congress report promises a social security system covering the whole population and reformed medical settlement, so the state is expected to guarantee basic care, though through a mixed insurance system.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Official doctrine stresses raising incomes and the middle-income group and adjusting wage mechanisms, but a substantial minimum-wage rise is not a stated demand, so this is inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The market is given a decisive role in resource allocation, yet public ownership stays dominant and the state steers strategic sectors, so the claim that markets beat governments is rejected as stated.

public-ownership.rationale: The Party constitution holds that public ownership plays the dominant role, and the report pledges to unswervingly consolidate and develop the public sector.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Regulating excessive incomes and adjusting distribution fall under common prosperity, but the documents do not call for significantly higher wealth taxes, so the answer is inferred.

unions-good.rationale: Unions exist only under Party-led structures such as the official federation, and independent unions are not accepted, so adherents would affirm worker representation without endorsing unions as independent bodies.

property-fundamental.rationale: Private property rights are protected and the private economy is supported, but property is subordinate to public ownership and the Party, so it is not a near-inviolable fundamental right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The report calls for regulating capital, preventing its disorderly expansion and strengthening antitrust, consistent with a state that supervises the market.

cut-welfare.rationale: Official policy aims at a multi-tiered social security system for the whole population, so cutting welfare as a dependency problem runs against the stated line.

worker-ownership.rationale: Public ownership by the state and collective ownership are the stated forms, not direct worker ownership of individual firms, though workers are described as masters of the state.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The comprehensive national security outlook gives priority to security, and surveillance for counter-terrorism is not treated as a rights problem in official doctrine.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The Party has not addressed recreational drug legalisation as doctrine; its governance emphasis on social order and moral health makes legalisation an unlikely position.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Official doctrine favours managing speech through a healthy online environment and unity among ethnic groups, so legal restriction is an inferred fit, though hate speech as such is not addressed.

strong-leader.rationale: Party doctrine stresses the leadership core and the authority of the Party Central Committee, and treats unified leadership as a strength over gridlock, though framed as a Party, not an individual, matter.

state-harmful.rationale: The state is the instrument of the people's democratic dictatorship and is to be strengthened, so the idea that it is harmful is rejected outright.

limit-guns.rationale: Strict state control of firearms is an unquestioned feature of governance, but gun policy is not an ideological topic in the documents, so this is inferred from order and security priorities.

empower-police-military.rationale: The report calls for modernising the armed forces to world-class standards by mid-century and for strong public security capacity.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Sex work is illegal and treated as a social ill under socialist moral norms; the documents do not discuss it, so this is inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: The Party stresses democratic centralism and unified leadership from the centre, with local authorities subordinate to central decisions.

rehabilitation.rationale: Official legal doctrine blends punishment and reform of offenders; the documents do not settle the emphasis.

traditional-family.rationale: Official ideology promotes fine traditional culture and family virtues, and Xi era doctrine emphasises family values and childbirth support.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The state does not recognise same-sex marriage and official doctrine stresses traditional family values, though the topic is not formal doctrine; inferred.

abortion-legal.rationale: Abortion is legal in China, but recent policy aims to raise births, so adherents are not firmly on one side; inferred.

more-religion-public.rationale: The CCP is atheist, bars members from religion, and requires religions to adapt to socialist society, so a larger public role is not wanted.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Official doctrine addresses ethnic equality and development of minority regions but does not frame redress of historical racial injustice as a goal.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Gender equality is a stated aim but the social-construct theory is not official doctrine, and traditional family emphasis points the other way.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The report and Xi era doctrine call for carrying forward fine traditional Chinese culture and cultural confidence as part of the Party's mission.

gradual-change.rationale: The doctrine pairs stability and gradual reform with a revolutionary self-image and a goal of national rejuvenation, so adherents are split on this framing.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration is not an ideological issue in the documents; China has little immigration and doctrine is silent, so the position is neutral.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: China backs the UN as central but stresses sovereignty and non-interference, and promotes its own initiatives rather than greater supranational power.

free-trade.rationale: The report supports opening up and a global network of partnerships while the state steers strategic industries; "benefits everyone" is not a doctrinal claim.

nation-first.rationale: Doctrine puts national rejuvenation and sovereignty first yet also claims to promote a community with a shared future for mankind, so adherents are split on the framing.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The independent foreign policy of peace is built on non-interference and opposition to hegemonism, so intervention to protect human rights is rejected.

open-borders.rationale: Sovereignty and national territorial integrity are central, and open borders have no place in doctrine despite the communist ultimate goal.

limit-growth.rationale: Development is the first priority and Deng held that socialism cannot endure if it remains poor, though green development is promoted alongside it.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The report commits to peak and neutrality goals and ecological civilization, but frames the transition as phased and keeps coal in use, so support is real but measured.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Science and technology are called the primary productive force and self-reliance in technology is a strategic priority.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The report says to develop nuclear power actively, safely and in an orderly manner.

revolution-justified.rationale: The Party came to power by revolution and its constitution celebrates it, though today it opposes revolution against its own rule.

experts-over-public.rationale: Doctrine stresses scientific decision-making and technocratic leadership but ultimate authority is the Party, not experts or the public.

central-planning.rationale: The post-1978 line is a socialist market economy with a decisive market role, though the state plans strategically; pure central planning is not the model.

socialized-markets.rationale: The official model combines markets with dominant public ownership, which matches the claim as stated.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land is state or collectively owned in China and land-value taxation is not part of doctrine, so this is inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Regulating excessive incomes is part of common prosperity, but inheritance taxation is not a stated position.

basic-income.rationale: Doctrine favours work and tiered social security, not unconditional universal payments; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The report stresses self-reliance and industrial strengthening while upholding opening up, so protectionism is neither endorsed nor rejected explicitly.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The report promotes strategic emerging industries and the leading role of the state sector, with the state guiding investment toward national goals.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Public ownership is dominant and diverse ownership forms coexist, so widely spread small property is not the stated aim.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Communism is the highest ideal and ultimate goal in the constitution, though abolition is placed in a distant future and distribution by work stays dominant now.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The financial system is state controlled and central banks are instruments of macroeconomic management in doctrine.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Official federations exist under Party leadership but the model is Party-led socialism, not tripartite price-setting bodies; inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Party is the core of leadership and party leadership is the defining feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics, one of the Four Cardinal Principles.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Doctrine is republican, anti-feudal and rests on the people's democratic dictatorship, so hereditary rule is not legitimate.

democracy-best.rationale: The Party calls whole-process people's democracy the broadest and most genuine form but rejects liberal democracy as a universal model, and puts stability before voters' choices.

direct-votes.rationale: Democracy is exercised through people's congresses under Party leadership, and referendums are not part of the system.

workers-councils.rationale: Power runs through the Party, people's congresses and democratic centralism, not workers' councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: Territorial integrity is a core principle and the report opposes separatism, so secession rights are rejected.

natural-rulers.rationale: The Party sees itself as the vanguard that should rule by merit and conviction, but does not claim people are naturally suited to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Party's founding legitimacy rests on armed revolution, and the state holds that violence is legitimate in the name of the people.

war-builds-character.rationale: Doctrine stresses peaceful development and opposition to hegemonism, though the armed forces are to be ready for struggle; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: Freedom of belief is constitutional, yet religions must be Sinicised and adapt to socialist society under Party supervision, so the separation is neither strict nor absent.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The Party is atheist and law derives from the Party-led socialist rule of law with Chinese characteristics.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Courts, police and army are state and Party organs, and the armed forces answer to Party command.

military-superiority.rationale: The report sets the goal of world-class armed forces by mid-century, though official language rejects hegemony and calls the posture defensive.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The state is described as multi-ethnic with equality and unity among groups and regional ethnic autonomy, though Han-centred nationalist tendencies exist.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Marxist-Leninist tradition holds this, though the reform era holds class struggle is no longer the main contradiction.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Common prosperity is a defining feature, but doctrine says it is not egalitarianism and keeps distribution according to work dominant.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Regional ethnic autonomy exists under central authority, but land authority for indigenous peoples is not a stated position.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The Party's narrative stresses the century of humiliation, but reparations as a demand are not stated in the documents.

civilizational-union.rationale: Doctrine is about a Chinese nation and a community of shared future, not unions based on shared religion or civilisation.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Official ideology promotes socialist core values, collectivism and service to the people, rejecting selfishness.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Socialist collectivism and the Chinese path of human rights stress the right to development and duties to the community over individual rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Ecological civilization speaks of lucid waters and lush mountains as invaluable assets, mixing intrinsic and instrumental value.

limit-population.rationale: The past one-child policy has been reversed and the report notes birth policy adjustments, so population limits are no longer the line.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Doctrine champions industrial modernisation and the primary productive forces, and rejects rolling back industry.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Technology-led self-reliance is a priority, though under the Party's stability priority, so disruption of existing institutions is not welcomed.

human-enhancement.rationale: There is no documented position; state regulation of biotechnology is emphasised.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Digital governance is promoted but decision-making remains Party-led; doctrine does not address AI takeover.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Comprehensive cyberspace management and a security first approach oppose encryption the state cannot access.

restore-past-order.rationale: Doctrine is forward-looking, modernising and revolutionary; it draws on tradition only to support national rejuvenation.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Deng's pragmatism says policy by results, yet the Party insists ideology must guide and rejects the claim it lacks ideology, so adherents are split.

direct-action.rationale: Political change is to come through the Party and state institutions; unauthorised direct action against the order is not accepted.

means-match-ends.rationale: Marxism-Leninism accepts that means may differ from the end state, as in the dictatorship of the proletariat; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Doctrine is committed to industrial modernisation and the development of productive forces.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Marxist doctrine envisions abolishing the division of labour under communism in the far future, but it is not a present programme.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The constitution says communism is the ultimate goal, while distribution according to work dominates for now.

production-for-use.rationale: The ultimate goal is communist production for needs, but the current market economy remains profit driven; adherents hold this as a distant principle.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The classical doctrine speaks of exploitation, but the Party now welcomes private entrepreneurs, and the Three Represents admitted capitalists.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The people's democratic dictatorship is a Four Cardinal Principle and is officially described as essentially the dictatorship of the proletariat.

collective-farming.rationale: Collective land ownership persists but household contract farming replaced communes after 1978, so adherents are split.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Marxism-Leninism holds capitalism leads to imperialism, and the CCP views capitalist powers' hegemonism as a source of conflict.

taxation-theft.rationale: The state's authority to tax is basic to the socialist state and its public provision.

harm-principle.rationale: The state may restrict individual actions on grounds of order, morality and the public interest, not only harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Official doctrine rejects the Western individual-rights model in favour of the collective and development rights.

conscription.rationale: Military service is a constitutional duty in China, and conscription law is in place.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Doctrine values the Party's leadership and sees no need to compare exit to voting as a check on government.

state-as-business.rationale: Governance is Party-led service to the people, not a customer model, though efficient management is valued.

positive-liberty.rationale: The right to subsistence and development is placed first in the official human rights discourse, matching a material view of freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: Official doctrine controls media and academia under Party leadership; the claim that they outrank officials is rejected.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Marxism-Leninism rejects biological theories of racial difference and stresses equality among ethnic groups.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation is through people's congresses and the Party, with mass organisations under its leadership, not an organic corporatist model.

total-state.rationale: The Party leads all areas including education, culture and economy, but the economy is partly market based and the state does not claim to run all life.

national-rebirth.rationale: National rejuvenation of the Chinese nation after the century of humiliation is the Party's central mission and a Xi Jinping slogan.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Official doctrine denies hegemonism and expansionism and claims defensive aims, though it presses claims to Taiwan and disputed seas.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Doctrine is rule by Party institutions and law, not feudal oaths of personal loyalty.

bound-labor.rationale: Bound labour is feudal and opposed by the Party's revolutionary history and its land reform.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Marxism treats knowledge as class based, and officials argue that ideology and academia must serve the people under Party leadership.

universal-morality.rationale: The Party rejects universal values as Western and ties morality to class and socialist core values.

single-common-good.rationale: The Party claims to represent the fundamental interests of all the people and to pursue the common good as defined by its leadership.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The Party's stance on Israel is not part of ideology and the documents do not address the claim.

revive-national-language.rationale: Standard Mandarin is promoted as the national language and no revival of a lost language is part of doctrine; inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Workers as masters of the state are celebrated and worker congresses exist in state firms, but the doctrine gives no strong programme.

school-vouchers.rationale: State provision of education is the model, and market-style vouchers are not part of doctrine; inferred.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal stance is pragmatic, using stimulus when needed; it is not an ideological commitment either way.

economic-freedom.rationale: The Party holds that political leadership comes first and rejects the claim that political freedom depends on economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Moral example by Party members is stressed alongside law, so this is split.

national-self-determination.rationale: Marxism-Leninism supports national liberation and China's own sovereignty, but opposes it when invoked for Taiwan, Tibet or Xinjiang.

force-without-un.rationale: China upholds the UN as central and condemns unilateral use of force by other states.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The Party is committed to scientific materialism and atheism, but the claim that reason alone should guide is stronger than doctrine; inferred.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Social welfare in China is tied to residence and citizenship, but immigrants are not discussed in the documents.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The report favours a social safety net with promoting employment; doctrine does not prescribe work requirements.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Three Represents admitted private entrepreneurs, and the harmonious society doctrine favours cooperation over class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The Party now calls for carrying forward fine traditional culture, reversing the Mao era's attacks.

dominated-front.rationale: China fosters ties with the Global South and a global network of partnerships, but avoids forming blocs against particular countries.

workers-nation.rationale: Doctrine unites patriotism with socialism and stresses a nation-centred line under Party leadership rather than a purely international class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Gender equality is a constitutional principle, and equal participation of women in public life is official policy.

ban-interest.rationale: The state runs a banking and credit system and interest is part of it.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Official doctrine requires equality, unity and mutual assistance among ethnic groups.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The state is described as the people's democratic dictatorship, a Marxist-Leninist view of the state as a class instrument.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Coal is used more cleanly and energy security is stressed, while the report also sets carbon peak and neutrality goals.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Immigration is not addressed; the unity of ethnic groups is emphasised for minorities within China.

elite-replacement.rationale: There is no support for the replacement conspiracy theory in the doctrine.

proportional-representation.rationale: The Party rejects multiparty competition and uses people's congress delegates, not party-list proportional seats.

national-mission.rationale: The Party claims to offer China's solution and wisdom to world problems but says it does not export its model.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The Party holds that women's liberation is part of socialist development and equal, rather than endorsing structural patriarchy as a current feature.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The Party acknowledges corruption as a threat and campaigns against it, but rejects the notion that its leaders are out of touch.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: The documents do not support this; eugenics is not a stated position and modern law bars discrimination.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The Party's armed forces and security organs are under absolute Party command and not subject to legal accountability for past actions.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The state leads economic and social development, which is the opposite of the minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Official policy upholds equality and unity among groups, with no support for discouraging mixing.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equality of all citizens before the law is constitutional and class based distinctions in the people's dictatorship give it limits.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The doctrine is socialism with Chinese characteristics built in one country, the opposite of this claim.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed in the doctrine; the Party's anti-imperialist line supports national liberation movements generally.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: China has a uniform civil code while recognising ethnic autonomy regions; religion-specific law is not an issue in the documents.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The state restricts proselytising and unregistered religion, but conversion as such is not banned in doctrine.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Beef is common in China and there is no such position; inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The state is atheist and religious education in state schools is excluded, with schooling used for ideological teaching.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The CCP treats the state as a tool needing strengthening, with the army under the Party and a national security outlook against hostile forces.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Party claims legitimacy from the people's support and whole-process democracy, but rejects electoral consent as the test.

trade-surplus.rationale: The report aims at high level opening and does not state export surplus as doctrine.

population-transfer.rationale: Doctrine is for unity of ethnic groups and no stated policy of pressuring minorities to leave; there is no relevant statement.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Marxism-Leninism endorses revolutionary force and the state holds a monopoly on coercion.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Marxist doctrine sees class struggle and productive forces, not individual competition, as the engine, and stresses cooperation and harmony.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Hostile forces and subversion are to be cracked down on, and the Party bans opposition parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The republican concept is not part of Party doctrine; arbitrary power by the Party is not acknowledged.

separated-powers.rationale: Deng rejected separation of powers and official writings call Western constitutionalism incompatible with the people's democratic dictatorship.

vanguard-party.rationale: The constitution presents the Party as the vanguard of the working class, and it exercises leadership over all.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The Party promises common prosperity and poverty alleviation as a defining mission.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: The Chinese housing privatisation of the 1990s did this, but it is not a doctrinal commitment.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes are not protected in law and independent labour action is suppressed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Official doctrine sees poverty as caused by unbalanced development and has relaxed birth limits, and does not blame population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The Party celebrates unity of all ethnic groups as a strength though it suppresses separatism; inferred.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Offices are filled by Party organisation and people's congress election, with no lottery.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Emphasis on national security and cracking down on subversion supports emergency powers against internal enemies.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The state manages prices of essentials and reserves, though not stated as doctrine in the sources.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Party's leadership of ideological work and public opinion is official policy, with comprehensive cyberspace management.

party-commands-army.rationale: The constitution and report both state the Party's absolute leadership over the armed forces, a principle dating to the Gutian Congress.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation is rare and not discussed as doctrine.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Historic communist ideal from the Paris Commune, but not a stated current Chinese position.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Democratic centralism binds members to adopted decisions and the constitution demands strict discipline.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Doctrine defends national sovereignty and independence and opposes supranational limits.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The armed forces are under the Party Central Military Commission, not the head of state in a presidential sense, though the offices converge in practice.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not a doctrinal matter; the Party supervises religious bodies by state-approved associations.

clerical-rule.rationale: Clerical rule contradicts the Party's atheism and its own leadership role.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Leninist defeatism was early Marxist doctrine but the CCP stresses patriotism and does not endorse it.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Literature and art are to serve socialist values and the people, with content control in the cultural sphere.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The 2018 amendment removed term limits on the presidency, and Xi Jinping has been re-elected beyond two terms.

recall-officials.rationale: Delegates to people's congresses can be recalled in law, but the Party does not promote voter recall as doctrine.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: China opposes military blocs and exclusive groups against specific countries and has no standing alliances, though the report does not call for others to withdraw.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not stated in doctrine and rental housing is permitted.

people-in-arms.rationale: The People's Liberation Army is a professional force under the Party, and militia are a supplement, so replacement is rejected.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Rural revitalisation is promoted but urbanisation is also, so no moral claim is made.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reunification with Taiwan is a core goal of the Party, and the report says it will never renounce force.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The Party values the educated and intellectuals while requiring them to serve the people; there is no doctrine either way.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Doctrine claims no civilisation is superior and also praises fine traditional Chinese culture as especially valuable.

death-penalty.rationale: China retains capital punishment and it is accepted in law for grave crimes.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Gender equality is a principle and schools teach it, but sex education content is cautious; no doctrine.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The Party's scientific materialism means creationism has no place in schools.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Pornography is banned in China and a healthy online environment is official policy.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Chinese nationality law rests on descent, not birth on the territory.

minority-language-support.rationale: Regional ethnic autonomy includes use of minority languages, though Mandarin is promoted.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Religion must be Sinicised and subject to general law and Party supervision, so exemptions are not granted.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Social conformity to socialist core values is promoted, so eccentricity is not particularly encouraged.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: China is a creditor to poor countries and prefers renegotiation and its own initiatives; not a stated doctrine.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Marxism-Leninism links national independence to socialist transformation and the Party presents economic structure as decisive.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitutional change is done by the Party-led National People's Congress, and a democratically elected constituent assembly is not part of the system.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Deng and later leaders put stability and development ahead of Western-style political liberalisation.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: China pledges support to developing countries via its global initiatives but frames it as mutual cooperation; the claim as a duty is inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: China maintains its own nuclear forces and builds strategic deterrence as part of building world-class armed forces.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The head of state is elected by the National People's Congress, not directly, and direct election is not part of the system.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The central bank is under the State Council and Party leadership of finance is stressed.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Claimed national territory is non-negotiable in doctrine, with sovereignty and territorial integrity being core interests.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Private property is protected but subordinate to public ownership and the interests of the people as defined by the Party.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The Party sees the Soviet Union as a socialist state whose collapse came from ideological ossification and abandonment of Party leadership.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Ecological civilization stresses prevention but doctrine does not endorse the precautionary principle by name.

collective-defense.rationale: China opposes military blocs and its mutual defence treaty with North Korea is the exception, so the claim as general doctrine is rejected.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Doctrine does not address territories annexed by other countries as a general rule, and it treats its own claims as sovereignty.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Religions must be Sinicised, adapt to socialist society and are supervised by the state and Party.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The president is also the Party General Secretary, and a non-partisan head of state is not the model.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The report refuses to renounce force over Taiwan and opposes separatism.

region-keeps-system.rationale: One country, two systems is the official model for Hong Kong and Macao and the proposed model for Taiwan.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The Party is atheist and rejects the divine sanction of rulers.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Regulating excessive incomes and distribution support progressive taxation.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marxism holds that social being determines consciousness, so character comes from circumstances.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Party and everyone act within the Constitution and law in doctrine, though in practice Party leadership sits above legal institutions.

space-expansion.rationale: The space programme is a major prestige and technology project but not a stated central civilisational goal.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The people's democratic dictatorship is a single system of Party leadership and people's congresses, not a mixed constitution.

leader-cult.rationale: Official doctrine criticises the cult of personality since Mao, but Xi's image and the core leader language are promoted, so adherents are split.

equal-parenting.rationale: There is no stated position and the question is a matter of family law.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Mao held this, but the reform era says class struggle is no longer the main contradiction while it continues to exist within certain limits.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land reform was the Party's revolutionary programme, though it is historical and not current doctrine.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed in the documents; no position.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The Party's claim to Taiwan rests on sovereignty, not co-ethnic claims, and it stresses opposition to expansion.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Chinese law guarantees freedom of belief, including freedom to leave a religion, and the Party is atheist.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not a position of the Party, which opposes religious extremism and discourages religious dress control.

common-currency.rationale: The yuan is the national currency and monetary sovereignty is stressed, with no stated support for a shared currency.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Doctrine places the Chinese nation within its borders and does not seek union with kin peoples elsewhere.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Regional ethnic autonomy gives minorities limited self-government within the state, not a state of their own.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The Party supports integration in countries of residence for overseas Chinese and opposes separatism; the claim as written is inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism is the core of Marxism-Leninism, which the Party upholds as its theoretical foundation.

ban-cartels.rationale: The report supports strengthening antitrust and preventing disorderly expansion of capital.

no-bailouts.rationale: State owned banks and firms are supported by the state, so bailouts are used, though not stated as doctrine.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Courts answer to people's congresses and the Party, so the claim is not a doctrinal fit for liberal democracies.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Women are guaranteed representation shares in congresses, but equal quotas are not doctrine.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Self-reliance in key technologies is stressed together with high-level opening up, so a shut-off bloc is not doctrine.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: China emphasises non-interference and development and does not push binding linkage; inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: The ideology stresses ideals, conviction and serving the people, though material incentives are the main spur since Deng.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Maoist armed struggle in the countryside is part of the Party's own history but it does not promote this for others.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Party's revolution was anti-feudal and abolished hereditary titles.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Overseas Chinese are treated as compatriots, but there is no stated right of return policy in the documents.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The Party stresses education about Chinese history and cultural confidence, with political education in the curriculum from primary school to university.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Doctrine is anti-imperialist and condemns colonial domination, so tutelage is rejected.

patriotic-education.rationale: The report calls for fostering love for the Party and country, with patriotism as a core of ideology and political education throughout schooling.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Minority preferences in education exist as policy for ethnic autonomy regions; not doctrine, inferred.

public-money-creation.rationale: The state-owned central bank and banks create money under state control; inferred from state control of finance.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Marxism-Leninism says socialism will inevitably replace capitalism, though the Party uses market mechanisms and sees capitalist crises.

former-empire-influence.rationale: National rejuvenation and the Taiwan and border claims draw on the Qing inheritance, so some cultivation of influence in historic spheres is inferred; the documents do not state it as a principle.

delink-world-market.rationale: The 20th Congress report commits to opening up and the socialist market economy, and rejects decoupling.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Marxist-Leninist lineage has a labor-aristocracy strand, but the current line casts workers as the leading class and does not treat them as exploiters; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: State-led common prosperity and Party control of society make the CCP hostile to unregulated private choice; no direct statement.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The CCP rejects liberal constitutionalism and separation of powers, and places the Party above entrenched checks.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The official narrative of national humiliation condemns unequal treaties imposed on China, but void-today claims for others are inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: Official doctrine rejects hereditary rule and calls its system a people's democracy with elected congresses; this is inferred.

minority-veto.rationale: Democratic centralism requires the minority to submit to the majority and lower bodies to higher ones, so a minority veto is rejected.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The Party constitution demands leadership of everything and rejects Western checks on it; a right to resist rulers is inferred as rejected.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The National People's Congress is the highest organ of state power in the constitution, and monarchy is rejected, though the Party leads it.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: The ecological civilisation line values nature, but animal sentience is not part of official doctrine; adherents are inferred as indifferent.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Official policy treats animals as a resource for farming and research with welfare limits; this is inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Common prosperity and calls for the wealthy to give back imply duties toward the less fortunate, inferred from official speeches.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The Party constitution obliges members to take an active part in political and social work, ruling out withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Marxist-Leninist theory holds ideology serves the dominant class; official doctrine applies this to capitalist societies, so this is inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Marxism-Leninism stresses both force and ideology in class rule, so adherents are inferred to be split on the word mainly.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Leninist theory of imperialism holds the core exploits the periphery, though the Party also endorses globalisation, so the lean is mild.

native-born-offices.rationale: The doctrine addresses citizenship and nationality equally, not birthplace; this is inferred as neutral.

party-own-road.rationale: The Party constitution upholds independence, equality and non-interference between parties and promotes socialism with Chinese characteristics.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Official policy embraces opening up and foreign investment alongside self-reliance in key technology, so the claim is mildly rejected.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The report treats reunification and recovering lost land as a national mission, though the cases are not all territory lost in war.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Doctrine stresses equality and unity of all ethnic groups under Party leadership, so ancestry-based leadership is rejected; inferred.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The Party's legitimacy narrative celebrates victory in the anti-fascist war, but making it a constitutional founding value is inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Official doctrine rejects equating communism with fascism as a Western anti-communist trope; inferred from its stance.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Marxist doctrine reads the Civil War as a struggle against slavery, so denial is rejected; this is inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The Party removes some symbols and preserves others for political reasons; adherents have no settled position, so this is inferred as split.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the official line stresses women's equality but not male disadvantage.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The domestic violence law is gender-neutral on paper, but official doctrine does not take a clear position on symmetry.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The report states China will not copy Western political models and follows its own path of modernisation, a central official theme.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The Party constitution subordinates the armed forces to the Party's absolute leadership, so an independent guardian role is rejected.

paid-care-work.rationale: The doctrine stresses socialised care services but does not call for paying domestic labour; inferred as a mild disagreement.

filial-duty.rationale: The Party promotes traditional Chinese culture and family virtues under cultural confidence, and Chinese law imposes a duty of adult children to support parents; the 20th Congress report stresses family values and elder care.

office-by-exam.rationale: The Party selects cadres by Party organisation, with civil-service examinations used for entry; it rejects election-based selection as the sole route but does not hold exams to be the principle, so it is split.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The 20th Congress report stresses national security, self-reliance in key technologies and safe industrial and supply chains, and the state keeps control of strategic sectors under dominant public ownership.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The documents do not address divorce procedure; the Party stresses family stability, but Chinese law already allows divorce by mutual consent, so the position is unclear.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The Party rejects multiparty and Western-style electoral democracy and rests on democratic centralism, under which leaders are chosen and directed within the Party hierarchy, not bound and recalled by voters; the Paris Commune model appears only as heritage.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from the report's plan for a multi-tiered social security system with public basic pensions; private individual accounts are a supplementary tier, not the replacement for the state system.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land in China is publicly owned (state or collective) and held by users under use rights, and the Party Constitution commits to dominant public ownership.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The National People's Congress is formally the organ that approves the budget, which the Party presents as part of whole-process people's democracy, though under Party leadership and without genuine checking.

single-official-language.rationale: The Party promotes Putonghua and the national common language and script as part of forging a sense of community of the Chinese nation, as the 20th Congress report says.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: All land is publicly owned, so no one, foreign or domestic, owns it outright; the position follows from the public-ownership principle in the Party Constitution.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred: the Party frames equality through common prosperity and ethnic unity and rejects Western race-based identity politics; the documents do not address the legal test.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The Party promotes domestic consumption as a growth driver while also advocating frugality and opposing waste and hedonism, so the line is mixed.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Official doctrine opposes interference in other countries' internal affairs and hegemonism, as the 20th Congress report states; Mao-era support for insurgencies is a historical departure.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Official foreign policy rests on non-interference and opposes hegemonism, though historical Soviet-bloc interventions drew support from Mao-era thinking; the current line condemns such action as great-power bullying.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from official calls to 'regulate capital' and prevent its disorderly expansion under Party leadership.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the Party's emphasis on national security and sovereignty against foreign interference.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The 20th Congress report commits to improving population and birth policies to counter low fertility.

residents-only-property.rationale: Official documents do not address residency-based property rules; adherents' position is unclear.

job-guarantee.rationale: The report adopts an employment-first policy and aims at fuller and higher-quality employment.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred from the Party's rejection of liberal democracy and Western democracy promotion.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The Party leads rule of law and the state is a people's democratic dictatorship, with no right to disobey Party-led law.

non-intervention.rationale: The report opposes interference in other countries' internal affairs, in line with the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not addressed in the sources; inferred as neutral.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred from the official line of ethnic unity and forging a common Chinese national community.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from official promotion of the family and marriage as foundations of society.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The Party promotes open government information in principle but also secrecy over state and Party matters, so inferred as split.

local-production.rationale: The sources do not address local production; the official line stresses a unified national market.

informal-organisation.rationale: Under Leninist democratic centralism the Party leads all organisation and does not tolerate independent informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The report stresses sovereignty and rejects external rule-setting, though China also cites international law selectively.

religious-nation.rationale: The Party is officially atheist and promotes the Sinicisation of religion under Party leadership.

missingStatements.text: Religions in the country should adapt to the society's political system and be led in a nationally oriented direction.
missingStatements.rationale: The report requires religions to be Chinese in orientation and adapt to socialist society.

missingStatements.text: A government should treat development and poverty reduction as the first human right.
missingStatements.rationale: The report commits to a Chinese path of human rights development centred on subsistence and development.

notes: Several answers on social and moral issues are inferred because Party documents are silent; Wikipedia's article is the only secondary source opened, and the Party Constitution page was read only for its General Program.
